today.name: Rill Browser
today.tagline: The browser where Claude Code and Codex work beside you
today.description: Rill is an AI-native browser built around the Claude Code and Codex you already use. Browse normally, then press ⌘E on any page to turn what you're looking at into a task for your agent. Rill finds the right project, passes along the context, and the agent works while you keep browsing. It also sorts your tabs into themes, turns your history into days you can search, and brings every project your agents are working on into one place. Free, on the plan you already have.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm William! I made Rill because I want to always stay in the flow. As an ADHD, I never liked code-switching. My best ideas for work come when I'm supposedly not working at all: watching something for fun, reading things and following a rabbit hole, looking at how someone else solved a problem. Then when an idea hit me, I'd have to stop, switch to coding agents, find the project and explain it all, and most of the time I just didn't.Rill is my way of removing that code-switching. It's a browser with your Claude Code or Codex working alongside you. When something on a page gives you an idea, you say so right there, and an agent starts on it in the right project. You don't have to spend time looking for the right folder, rephrasing everything you just saw on the web, and you don't switch in and out of work mode. The work goes on with you in the flow.This matters now more than ever. Agents have shortened the distance between ideas to output near zero. So the bottleneck is capturing the idea at the moment you have it. That moment is nearly always while you're taking something in, and that is what a browser is for.Rill is a free AI-native browser. It's WebKit-based, which means it's native to Mac. And it runs on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have, so you don't have to buy a new subscription for all of its agentic capabilities.cHow do you keep an idea today when it shows up at the wrong time?

today.name: AUDR by Chargebee
today.tagline: Open standard for tracking agent run costs
today.description: AUDR (Agent Usage Detail Record) is an open standard, for capturing who initiated an agent run and what it cost across every system that run touches. Inspired by the telecom industry's Call Detail Record, AUDR defines a common JSON schema that any harness, router, or billing system can emit and ingest. Three core rules make it work: a shared run ID minted by the harness, clear field ownership, and strict merge rules where conflicts are rejected and corrections are new records.

today.name: Ghostifier
today.tagline: Companies have your data. Ghostifier gets them to delete it.
today.description: Instead of one form per company, Ghostifier starts from your inbox. It finds who holds your data, unsubscribes you and opts you out of sale and sharing on day one, waits out the return window, then sends deletion requests and tracks every reply. Banks, insurers and your employer are left alone. It also asks data brokers to delete you. Gmail access is headers only, so it never reads your email bodies, and there is no AI: every decision follows fixed rules.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Jonathan, and I built Ghostifier because I have a passion for technology and building tools, especially tools that work for me. I was overwhelmed with the constant inbox management, opting out of emails, unsubscribing, etc. but I knew those companies still stored my data. In an era of privacy and security, I wanted to go once step further. How it works: connect Gmail and it finds the companies that hold your data. Day one, it unsubscribes you and opts you out of sale and sharing. It then waits out the return window, so it doesn't cut off a refund, and only then sends a deletion request and tracks the reply. Banks, insurers, healthcare, schools, government and your employer are never sent one. What I think is different: It starts from your inbox, so you don't have to remember who has your data. You see what it will do before it does it, or switch on Autopilot. I build a one time scan / delete option as well as a continuous "always on" auto plan that will be your personal Ghosting Assistant. The scan is free; sending requests is on a paid plan. I'd love to hear which companies you'd want cleared first, and where the flow felt unclear.

month.description: Voiskey starts from what you meant, not just what you said. Speak a rough thought and it comes back shaped for where it's going and who's reading it: casual with a friend, composed with a colleague, technical with an AI. It arrives 5x faster than typing, cleaned up and ready to send, while you still sound like you. Voiskey is now available on iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows, in over 100 languages. comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Jenny, from the Voiskey team. We started this because of the same wall we kept hitting - AI dictation still isn't truly edit-free. The text comes out polished, and a lot of the time sanded flat: a message to a friend comes back like a memo, or a note to a colleague comes back like a template. None of it sounds like you, so you have to go back in and manually re-edit it before you send it. That's what Voiskey is built around. We called it "expression intelligence". Voiskey doesn't just catching your words. It works out what you meant, who's going to read it, and how you'd have put it yourself. The polish moves. Your voice stays. Why Voiskey: * Fits the moment. Reads the situation you're writing into and adjusts how the text comes out. * Keeps your voice. Your slang, your shorthand, and your way of putting things stay. * Learns your words. Remembers the names and terms you correct, so you fix them once. * Translates as you speak. Say it in your language, send it in theirs. It reads native, not translated. * Ask AI. Say what you want written and it lands in the field. Ask a question and the answer opens in a window. It's free to try, and there's a free month of Pro during launch. We'd love to hear what you think!

Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect.
